events.text: The clouds over the gate of {rgs_gate} part, and {rgs_name} is standing in the rain: {rgs_rel}, as you last saw them, before the death you could not stop. The lightning waits behind them like a servant. "You were going to go up without me," {rgs_name} says, not angrily. Only sure of it.

choices.text: Forgive yourself, in front of them

effects.log: You say the words you never said at the grave. {rgs_name} listens to all of them, and then the rain is only rain.

choices.text: Hold your mind against the shape

ok.log: You hold your heart still until the shape is only cloud wearing a face. It breaks like mist.

fail.log: The face holds, and the grief comes through your guard like a blade. You stagger, and the storm grows.

choices.text: Look away from them

effects.log: You look away. When you look back they are gone, and the storm is heavier by exactly one person.

events.text: In the storm over the gate of {rgs_gate} you see {rgs_name}, {rgs_rel}, standing with folded hands the way they always stood when you had done something foolish. They died before their time, and you were not there. "So," {rgs_name} says, "this is where all that training went."

choices.text: Bow to them, and ask their pardon

effects.log: You kneel in the rain and bow the full nine times. {rgs_name} sighs, the old sigh, and lays a hand on your head. Then there is only rain.

choices.text: Show them what you became

ok.log: You stand and show every form you know, against the storm itself. The shape watches, nods once, and is gone.

fail.log: Your forms falter under their eyes as they never did under anyone else's. The shape shakes its head, and the storm thickens.

choices.text: Tell them you were busy

effects.log: The words sound worse in the storm than they did in your head. The shape does not answer. It does not leave either, until you do.

events.text: The face in the clouds over the gate of {rgs_gate} is {rgs_name}, {rgs_rel}, laughing the way they laughed the night before it ended. The lightning around them is almost gentle. "You still owe me a drink," {rgs_name} says. "Where you are going, I hear they do not serve it."

choices.text: Pour the drink they are owed

effects.log: You pour wine into the rain from the gourd at your belt. {rgs_name} drinks it, somehow, and grins, and is gone.

choices.text: Wave the shape back into the clouds

ok.log: You lift a hand and the shape thins, like breath on a cold morning. It goes without a word.

fail.log: Your hand shakes. The shape keeps laughing, and the storm leans in to listen.

choices.text: Walk past them

effects.log: You walk past. The laughter follows you all the way to the gate, and then it is thunder.

They look curious, as if they have been waiting a long time to ask you something. "Was it worth it?" {rgs_name} asks. "Tell me honestly. I have the time."

effects.log: You say nothing. {rgs_name} nods, as if that is an answer too, and the clouds close behind them, darker.

events.text: This face you do not know, and you know it at once: {rgs_name}, someone your soul loved in another life and failed to save. The storm over the gate of {rgs_gate} has brought them across lives to stand in front of you. "You did come back," {rgs_name} says. "I wondered if you would."

choices.text: Tell them you are sorry, across every life

effects.log: You do not remember the life. Your soul does. It says sorry through your mouth, in words older than you, and {rgs_name} bows.

choices.text: Steady yourself and let them go

ok.log: You breathe until the face is only a face, and let it go back into the clouds. It goes kindly.

fail.log: The face undoes you. You did not know you could grieve someone you never met. The storm feeds on it.

choices.text: Tell them you are not that person any more

effects.log: "No," {rgs_name} agrees. "You are not." The shape fades. The storm does not.

events.text: The storm over the gate of {rgs_gate} is full of faces you have never seen: dozens, hundreds, the people a past life of yours wronged and never repaid. They do not shout. They simply stand between you and the gate, and wait to see what you will do about them.

choices.text: Bow to each of them, one by one

effects.log: It takes all night. You bow to every face until your back aches, and one by one they step aside.

choices.text: Push through them by will alone

ok.log: You walk through the crowd like a ship through fog, and the faces part.

fail.log: The crowd holds. Every step costs you, and the storm is thicker for every face you could not pass.

choices.text: Go around them

effects.log: There is no way around. You find this out slowly, and the storm grows while you look.

events.text: In the heart of the storm over the gate of {rgs_gate} there is a face you know best of all: your own, older, colder, everything the dark in your heart would make of you. It is very calm. "Go up like this," it says, "and you will be me in a hundred years. Why wait?"

choices.text: Forgive the dark in yourself

effects.log: You do not fight it. You tell it that you know it, and that you are not afraid of it. It goes quiet, like a dog that has been named.

choices.text: Cut it out of the storm

effects.log: You pretend. It does not. It walks beside you to the gate, smiling.
